component.name: cxf
component.title: CXF
component.description: Expose SOAP services, or invoke operations of SOAP services, using Apache CXF. The dataFormat option decides how the SOAP message is represented in the Camel message body.
component.label: http,webservice

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

synchronous.label: producer,advanced
synchronous.description: Whether to always process the exchange synchronously. If true, the producer invokes the CXF Client without a callback and waits until the invocation returns, and the consumer runs the route without a CXF continuation. The component sets the value on each endpoint that it creates, including a bean: endpoint, unless the endpoint URI sets synchronous.

allowStreaming.label: advanced
allowStreaming.description: Whether to allow CXF to keep the last message part of an incoming SOAP message as a javax.xml.transform.Source read from the stream, instead of parsing it into a DOM. Only used when dataFormat is PAYLOAD. The component sets the value on each endpoint that it creates, including a bean: endpoint, unless the endpoint URI sets allowStreaming. If not set, an endpoint that has no allowStreaming value uses the JVM system property org.apache.camel.component.cxf.streaming, and allows streaming when that property is not set either.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

headerFilterStrategy.label: filter
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.spi.HeaderFilterStrategy to filter header to and from Camel message.

useGlobalSslContextParameters.label: security
useGlobalSslContextParameters.description: Whether to use the global SSL context parameters of the CamelContext for each endpoint that the component creates and that has no sslContextParameters. The producer uses them for the HTTPS requests that it sends. The consumer does not use them.

CamelCxfOperationNamespace.description: The namespace of the operation named by the CamelCxfOperationName header or by defaultOperationName. The producer uses it in place of defaultOperationNamespace to find the operation to invoke. The consumer sets it to the namespace of the operation of the request. It is not set when dataFormat is RAW.

CamelDestinationOverrideUrl.description: The address that the producer sends the request to, in place of the service address. With the cxf component, the HTTP transport of CXF uses it, and the Camel transport does not.

ResponseContext.description: The CXF response context, as a Map. The producer sets it on the Camel message of the response. It holds the CXF properties of the CXF response message, for example the response code. The consumer copies its entries to the CXF response message, but exchange properties and values from the Camel message headers replace entries with the same key. The entry org.apache.cxf.message.Message.PROTOCOL_HEADERS is not used, because the consumer builds the protocol headers from the Camel message headers.

CamelAuthentication.description: The authenticated user of the request, as a Subject. The consumer sets it from the SecurityContext of the CXF request message: the Subject of a LoginSecurityContext, or else a new Subject with the user Principal.

RequestContext.description: The entries to add to the CXF request context, as a Map. The producer copies them to the CXF request context, but exchange properties and values from the Camel message headers replace entries with the same key. The entry org.apache.cxf.message.Message.PROTOCOL_HEADERS is not used, because the producer builds the protocol headers from the Camel message headers.

consumerOut.description: POJO: a MessageContentsList of the parameters of the operation, typed as the service class declares them, with its name in the CamelCxfOperationName header; null for an operation without parameters. PAYLOAD: a CxfPayload of the elements of the soap:Body and the SOAP headers. RAW: the stream of the whole SOAP envelope, without the operation name. CXF_MESSAGE: the SAAJ SOAPMessage

consumerReply.description: POJO: the return value of the operation, of the type the service class declares (a byte array is one value), or a List or an Object array of it and the out and holder parameters; another type is a SOAP fault, so the request MessageContentsList only fits an echo. PAYLOAD: a CxfPayload, or the XML of the soap:Body contents as text, bytes, a stream or a DOM. RAW: the whole SOAP envelope as text, bytes, a stream or a file. CXF_MESSAGE: a SOAPMessage, a javax.xml.transform Source, or the whole SOAP envelope as text, bytes, a stream or a DOM. A body that does not convert is a SOAP fault

producerIn.description: POJO: the parameters of the operation (the CamelCxfOperationName header or defaultOperationName) as a List (or another Collection) or an Object array, or the one parameter as the body; each of the type the service class declares. Any other body, such as text or a byte array, is the one parameter. PAYLOAD: a CxfPayload, or the XML of the soap:Body contents as text, bytes, a stream, a file or a DOM. RAW: the whole SOAP envelope. CXF_MESSAGE: a SOAPMessage, a javax.xml.transform Source, or the whole SOAP envelope as text, bytes, a stream or a DOM; another body fails

producerOut.description: POJO: a MessageContentsList with the return value of the operation first, then the out and holder parameters; null for a void operation, and the body unchanged for a one-way one. PAYLOAD: a CxfPayload of the soap:Body contents. RAW: the stream of the SOAP envelope of the response, read once. CXF_MESSAGE: the SAAJ SOAPMessage

beanId.description: The id of a CxfEndpoint bean in the registry to use as this endpoint. Written in the path of the endpoint URI in place of the service address, with the prefix bean:, for example bean:orderEndpoint. The component sets the options of the endpoint URI on that bean, so endpoint URIs with different options must not share one bean instance.

address.label: service
address.description: The service address, for example http://localhost:9000/orders. The consumer receives requests at this address, and the producer sends requests to it. The CamelDestinationOverrideUrl header replaces this address for a request that the producer sends over HTTP.

dataFormat.description: How the SOAP message is represented in the Camel message body. POJO: the parameters of the operation as Java objects (requires serviceClass). PAYLOAD: the contents of the soap:Body as a CxfPayload. RAW: the raw message stream from the transport layer, with most CXF interceptors removed, so SOAP headers are not available. CXF_MESSAGE: a SAAJ SOAPMessage, processed by the full set of CXF interceptors. MESSAGE is deprecated and is the same as RAW.

wrappedStyle.description: Whether to use the document-literal wrapped style instead of the document-literal bare style for the operations of serviceClass. Not used for RPC-style operations or when serviceClass is a Provider. Otherwise, if not set, CXF uses the parameterStyle of the SOAPBinding annotation, and the wrapped style when there is none. The consumer does not use it when dataFormat is CXF_MESSAGE.

muteException.label: consumer
muteException.description: Whether to hide the exception of a failed exchange from the client. If true, the fault that the consumer returns does not contain the class or the message of the exception. This does not apply to a CXF Fault or an exception with the WebFault annotation, nor to a Camel message body that is a Throwable or a CxfPayload with a soap:Fault.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

cookieHandler.label: producer
cookieHandler.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.http.base.cookie.CookieHandler to keep the cookies of an HTTP session between the requests that the producer sends. An InstanceCookieHandler keeps the cookies in the handler itself, and an ExchangeCookieHandler keeps them in an exchange property. The consumer does not use it.

defaultOperationName.label: producer
defaultOperationName.description: The name of the operation that the producer invokes. Used when the Camel message has no CamelCxfOperationName header. If neither the CamelCxfOperationName header nor this option is set, the producer invokes the first operation that CXF returns for the service, in an order that is not defined. If neither wsdlURL nor serviceClass is set, the producer sets this option to Invoke.

defaultOperationNamespace.label: producer
defaultOperationNamespace.description: The namespace of the operation named by the CamelCxfOperationName header or by defaultOperationName. Used when the Camel message has no CamelCxfOperationNamespace header. If neither the CamelCxfOperationNamespace header nor this option is set, the producer uses the namespace of the service, which is the namespace of serviceName when serviceName is set. If neither wsdlURL nor serviceClass is set, the producer sets this option to http://camel.apache.org/cxf/jaxws/dispatch.

hostnameVerifier.label: producer
hostnameVerifier.description: To use a custom javax.net.ssl.HostnameVerifier for the HTTPS requests that the producer sends. Not used for reading the WSDL that wsdlURL points to. The consumer does not use it.

sslContextParameters.label: producer
sslContextParameters.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.support.jsse.SSLContextParameters for the HTTPS requests that the producer sends. If not set, the component sets it to the global SSL context parameters when it creates the endpoint and its own useGlobalSslContextParameters option is true. Not used for reading the WSDL that wsdlURL points to. The consumer does not use it.

wrapped.label: producer
wrapped.description: Whether to invoke a document-literal wrapped operation in its wrapped form instead of its unwrapped form. If true and dataFormat is POJO, the Camel message body of the request must hold the wrapper object in place of the parameters of the operation. The consumer does not use it.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

synchronous.label: producer,advanced
synchronous.description: Whether to always process the exchange synchronously. If true, the producer invokes the CXF Client without a callback and waits until the invocation returns, and the consumer runs the route without a CXF continuation. The component sets it to the value of its own synchronous option when it creates the endpoint, including a bean: endpoint, unless the endpoint URI sets it.

allowStreaming.label: advanced
allowStreaming.description: Whether to allow CXF to keep the last message part of an incoming SOAP message as a javax.xml.transform.Source read from the stream, instead of parsing it into a DOM. Only used when dataFormat is PAYLOAD. The component sets it to the value of its own allowStreaming option when it creates the endpoint, including a bean: endpoint, unless the endpoint URI sets it. If not set, the endpoint uses the JVM system property org.apache.camel.component.cxf.streaming, and allows streaming when that property is not set either.

bus.label: advanced
bus.description: To use a custom configured CXF Bus.

continuationTimeout.label: advanced
continuationTimeout.description: The timeout in milliseconds of the CXF continuation that the consumer uses to process the exchange asynchronously. If it expires before the route has completed, the consumer returns a fault to the client and sets an ExchangeTimedOutException on the exchange. Use 0 for no timeout. Not used when synchronous is true or when the consumer gets no continuation from the transport, for example with the JMS transport.

cxfBinding.label: advanced
cxfBinding.description: To use a custom CxfBinding to control the binding between Camel Message and CXF Message.

cxfConfigurer.label: advanced
cxfConfigurer.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.component.cxf.jaxws.CxfConfigurer to configure CXF in Java code. Its configure method receives the CXF factory bean before the client or server is created, and configureClient and configureServer receive the created Client or Server.

defaultBus.label: advanced
defaultBus.description: Whether to set the Bus of this endpoint as the CXF default bus by calling BusFactory.setDefaultBus. This applies to a Bus set with the bus option as well as to a Bus that the endpoint creates.

headerFilterStrategy.label: advanced
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter header to and from Camel message.

mergeProtocolHeaders.label: advanced
mergeProtocolHeaders.description: Whether to copy a protocol header to the Camel message as one String instead of a List when it has more than one value. The values are joined by a comma and a space. This applies to the request that the consumer receives and to the response that the producer receives. Sets the exchange property CamelCxfProtocolHeadersMerged to true.

mtomEnabled.label: advanced
mtomEnabled.description: Whether to send SOAP messages with MTOM, so that CXF writes them as XOP packages. Sets the exchange property mtom-enabled to the value of this option. The producer copies the property to the CXF request message, and the consumer copies it to the CXF response message. When dataFormat is RAW, CXF does not write the Camel message body as an XOP package.

properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To set additional CXF options using the key/value pairs from the Map. For example to turn on stacktraces in SOAP faults, properties.faultStackTraceEnabled=true. This is a multi-value option with prefix: properties.

schemaValidationEnabled.label: advanced
schemaValidationEnabled.description: Whether to validate the incoming and outgoing SOAP messages of the endpoint against the XML schema of the service. Sets the CXF property schema-validation-enabled to the value of this option. If not set, CXF validates only when another setting enables validation, for example the SchemaValidation annotation on serviceClass. When dataFormat is RAW, CXF does not validate the messages.

skipPayloadMessagePartCheck.label: advanced
skipPayloadMessagePartCheck.description: Whether to skip the check that each element in the SOAP body matches the message part that the operation declares. Sets the CXF property soap.no.validate.parts to true. This is not XML schema validation, which schemaValidationEnabled controls. If dataFormat is PAYLOAD and neither wsdlURL nor serviceClass is set, the producer sets this option to true.

loggingFeatureEnabled.label: logging
loggingFeatureEnabled.description: Whether to add a LoggingFeature, which writes the incoming and outgoing SOAP messages of the endpoint to the log. The LoggingFeature writes them with SLF4J at INFO level to loggers whose names start with org.apache.cxf.services.

loggingSizeLimit.label: logging
loggingSizeLimit.description: The size limit at which CXF truncates a SOAP message in the log. Sets the limit of the LoggingFeature that the endpoint adds when loggingFeatureEnabled is true. Use -1 for no limit.

skipFaultLogging.label: logging
skipFaultLogging.description: Whether to skip the log entry that the PhaseInterceptorChain writes when an interceptor throws an exception, for example the exception of a failed exchange of the consumer. Sets the CXF property org.apache.cxf.logging.FaultListener to a FaultListener that skips this log entry.

password.label: security
password.description: The password for HTTP Basic authentication. The producer puts it, together with the user name, in the protocol header Authorization of its HTTP requests. Only used when the username option is set. Not used for reading the WSDL that wsdlURL points to. The consumer does not use it.

username.label: security
username.description: The user name for HTTP Basic authentication. The producer puts it, together with the password, in the protocol header Authorization of its HTTP requests. Only used when the password option is set. Not used for reading the WSDL that wsdlURL points to. The consumer does not use it.

bindingId.label: service
bindingId.description: The id of the CXF binding, which is a namespace URI, for example http://cxf.apache.org/bindings/xformat for the XML binding without a SOAP envelope. If not set, CXF uses the binding of the wsdl:port. The id http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap12/ selects SOAP 1.2 when there is no WSDL.

portName.label: service
portName.description: The WSDL port, which is the name attribute of the wsdl:port element. Written as a QName in the form {namespaceURI}localPart, for example {http://example.org/orders}OrderPort.

publishedEndpointUrl.label: service
publishedEndpointUrl.description: The address to publish in the WSDL that the consumer serves at the service address followed by ?wsdl. It replaces the location of the address element in the wsdl:port. Use it when clients reach the service through another address, for example when the service is behind a proxy.

serviceClass.label: service
serviceClass.description: The Java class of the service, for example a service endpoint interface or a class that implements one. Written as a fully qualified class name, for example org.example.orders.OrderService. Required when dataFormat is POJO, which is the default. Without a WSDL, CXF builds the service from this class.

serviceName.label: service
serviceName.description: The WSDL service, which is the name attribute of the wsdl:service element. Written as a QName in the form {namespaceURI}localPart, for example {http://example.org/orders}OrderService. If not set and wsdlURL points to a WSDL with one service, that service is used.

wsdlURL.label: service
wsdlURL.description: The location of the WSDL. Can be on the classpath, file system, or be hosted remotely.
